concept: Chip is a small capsule key on the case for filters and quick presets: a selectable chip latches down like an old radio key and lights its lamp, a removable chip carries its own round remove key, and none of them is ever orange.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Material filter chip with a tinted fill and a check icon when selected
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tinted fill spends colour on a selection, which P1 forbids, and the check icon swaps the mechanism for a web convention.

default_to_avoid.pattern: flat tag chip with an inline x that is only 16px wide
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tiny cross is not a part with a 44px hit area, so P3 makes the remove key a separate round key.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): band keys that latch down and stay down while their band is chosen
Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): rows of plain keys printed beside their function
system/refs/ref-01.png: FM/AM keys in the body colour beside the display (estimated from chat)

derivation.form: A chip is a small capsule key with corner.round, its word printed on it, 36px or 44px tall.

derivation.consequence: press drops height to 0 in 60–70ms, return runs on the material's spring
derivation.form: Pressing drops the chip by motion.press-travel; a selected chip stays down with no shadow, and deselecting returns it on the spring.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: Selection is shown by latched depth, a lit ink lamp and a medium word on the sunken face, never by orange or a tinted fill.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The sm chip and the 24px remove key each extend an invisible hit area to control.md, 44px.

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only
derivation.form: The word is type.label in regular weight, and medium when latched, with the medium width reserved so nothing reflows.

options.name: raised tag with a printed ring

variants.reason: A shows selection by the mechanism itself, a key that latches down with its lamp lit, so it needs no colour (P1) and reads in shape (P3); B's 2px ring is the same mark as the focus ring, and C's rail reads as pick-one, which is SegmentedControl's job.

root.why: The chip's outer span keeps the key and its remove key together as one inline part in a row of chips.

key.why: A capsule key of matte plastic that stands at the part height until pressed or latched down.

body.why: A removable chip is a capsule of plastic holding its word and a separate round remove key at the end.

sm.why: The small chip draws 36px tall for dense filter rows and keeps a 44px hit area around it.

md.why: The default chip is 44px tall, the smallest target every part in dial keeps.

lamp.why: A 6px lamp sits recessed when off and fills with full ink when latched, so selection never needs orange.

icon.why: An optional stroke icon is printed before the word in the same ink, never as the only identifier.

word.why: The printed word is the label size, regular weight, turning medium when latched within a reserved medium width.

remove.why: The remove key is a separate 24px round key whose hit area reaches 44px, so it cannot be hit by accident.

cross.why: The cross is printed with the 2px ink stroke on the remove key, at 4.5:1 or more against it.

hover.why: Hover darkens the printed ink one step and never lifts the key, because real keys do not rise.

active.why: Pressing drops the key by its travel and collapses its shadow underneath it, at once.

aria-pressed=true.why: A selected chip is latched: it stays down by its travel with no shadow, its lamp lit and its word medium.

focus-visible.why: Every part shows the same dark ring with a gap, so focus never depends on a colour change.

disabled.why: A disabled chip loses its height and fades to half, while its edge stays readable against the body.

data-disabled.why: The whole chip shows the not-allowed cursor when disabled, including the printed word around its keys.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the key changes position at once, with no travel on press and no spring return.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the key keeps a real border and the lamp fills solid when latched, so selection survives.

transform.why: The key travels down in 65ms and returns on the spring so a press reads as a physical stroke.

box-shadow.why: The cast shadow collapses with the press or latch and grows back with the return, following the single light.

color.why: The ink step on hover fades briefly so the change is a reply to the pointer, not a flash.

background-color.why: The lamp's on and off fades within the segment time, the same as a display segment switching.
